brief: Nomura argues AI is masking a rising US risk premium and debunks the TINA (there is no alternative to USD assets) thesis. The chain: the Fed has missed its inflation target for five years, deficits have pushed US debt and NIIP liabilities to near record shares of GDP, and trust in US policy has eroded, yet there are no clear signs of de-risking from USD assets. Nomura says the reason is AI: AI-driven equity gains have ballooned foreign holdings of US assets. The ratio of US NIIP liabilities to all ROW net creditor nations' NIIP assets has reached 80%, an extreme concentration. During the GFC and pandemic, NIIP liabilities rose and the USD appreciated, but mainly because US residents repatriated foreign holdings more aggressively than foreigners repatriated US holdings, not because foreign inflows increased. This pattern is poorly understood and underlies the TINA view. Nomura's simulation shows US portfolio liabilities are now so large that moderate foreign repatriation could outstrip declines in US portfolio assets, shrinking NIIP liabilities and depreciating the dollar if an AI setback hits. US portfolio assets would need to fall over 30%, a GFC-scale decline, to fully offset that.
